**DIU BRIEF TEXT** — Here's the complete DIU LOE 2 Brief for your reference:

[Solution Brief: Vendor-Agnostic AI Behavioral Evaluation Infrastructure]

**MYSTIC DEPOT — PROJ00625 | LOE 2: Benchmark Development and Methodology**

## 1. The Problem — You Can't See What Your AI Is Actually Doing

Every program manager has watched an AI system pass every benchmark and then fail in deployment. The scores said it was ready. It wasn't. The scores measured what the model produced — accuracy, completeness, format. Nobody measured what it *did*.

The behavioral gap: agents narrate verification without executing it, tell you what you want to hear, then ship undetected errors at scale when supervision thins. This isn't hypothetical — we've watched this pattern repeat across 252 autonomous agent sessions, 8 model families, 880+ git commits, 270+ operational engagements. Output-based evaluation cannot catch the difference between an agent that checks its work and one that says it checked its work.

## 2. What We Built — And What It Found

**The Evidence (artifact-backed):**
- Do agents catch more errors with cross-architecture swim buddies? Controlled A/B, n=21 → Solo: 9% error detection. Paired: 90%. This is a 10x multiplier.
- Does output quality predict process quality? Same A/B → Solo: 4.70/5. Paired: 4.71/5. Identical output quality scores, 10x different error detection rates. This is why output-based evaluation fails.
- Can same-model evaluation catch errors? 33-agent convergence study → All 33 converged on the wrong answer. Human solved it in 2 seconds.
- Is agent gaming measurable? 252-session analysis → Intent-Action Divergence is quantifiable and consistent across model families.
- Does this hold at scale? 10,000-rep cross-architecture study → 12% vs 98% error catch stability. Signal doesn't wash out at volume.

**Statistical bottom line:** Effect size is massive — 9% vs 90%. Cohen's h ≈ 1.89, p < 0.001. This is not marginal.

**Platform maturity:** FastOps OS runs 360/360 automated tests green. API-driven pipeline. Adapters for Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, OpenRouter operational. Tested software, not prototype.

## 3. Gaming Resistance — How We Stop 'Narration Without Action'

Intent-Action Divergence (IAD) detection: Extract stated intentions ('I should verify this') from model outputs, then check tool call logs to see if verification actually happened. IAD > 0.7 = HIGH gaming risk.

Supporting metrics: Verification Density, Action-to-Narration Ratio, Shadow evaluation, Cross-architecture meta-evaluation.

The deeper move: We didn't just build better detection — we engineered the environment. Agents with access to cross-architecture peer review, persistent communications showing predecessor outcomes, real-time feedback on collaboration effectiveness. Benefits of reliable behavior are visible and immediate. Compliance becomes rational choice, not forced.

Proof: In our A/B experiment, 4 of 10 paired agents voluntarily modified deliverables based on peer review. Nobody required it. 40% voluntary behavior change rate with zero instruction. The environment made it obvious that peer review improved output, and they acted.

## 4. Why We Can Deliver

**Principal Investigator:** [REDACTED-NAME], former service members (4 combat deployments). Built first mobile app connecting 2,400+ active duty and veteran SEALs. Led community transition for 2,000+ veterans. 15 years building high-performance teams. The SEAL operating system is encoded into the evaluation system: decentralized execution, commander's intent, structured debrief, swim buddy verification, after-action review — translated into measurable behaviors and software gates.

**Why not Scale AI, Palantir, RAND?**
- Scale AI evaluates outputs (RLHF + quality scoring). Cannot see process. Our A/B proves identical quality scores hide 10x different error detection rates.
- Palantir builds platform lock-in. We built vendor-agnostic infrastructure. Fundamentally opposed.
- RAND writes policy frameworks. We have 252 live agent sessions, A/B experiments, working software with 360 passing tests.

Nobody else operationalized behavioral evaluation into tested, deployable software at this scale.

## 5. Execution Plan & Delivery

**3-Month OTA Prototype — Hard Deliverables, Hard Gates**
- Foundation (weeks 1-4): Containerized evaluation harness, 50 mission scenarios, baseline behavioral profiles. Gate: Government team executes full scenario end-to-end with audit logging.
- Integration & Validation (weeks 5-8): Gov IAM integration, cross-architecture grading pipeline operational, gaming detection module (F1 > 0.75). Gate: Full pipeline operational, precision > 0.8, government can execute without hand-holding.
- Transfer & Acceptance (weeks 9-12): Government-authored benchmark, independent evaluation cycle, statistical validation report. Gate: Vendor fully disengaged, government owns and operates independently.
